Police may arrest without warrant a person committing a specified POHA offence in the officer's view; s.18(2) also covers suspected s.10(1) offences in prescribed circumstances.

name: Miscellaneous Offences (Public Order and Nuisance) Act 1906

arrestPower.summary: Police may arrest without warrant a person committing an offence under the Act in the officer's view. Some sections (e.g. s.22) carry their own arrest clause.

name: Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958

arrestPower.summary: Some sections expressly make the offence arrestable and non-bailable (e.g. s.6(4)). Otherwise CPC term defaults apply.

name: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act 2021
aliases: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act

arrestPower.summary: Every offence under Part 2 is an arrestable offence for the CPC 2010. Bail still follows the maximum term unless the Act says otherwise.
Several sections carry an express arrest clause (e.g. ss.18(5), 20(4), 36(4)). Check each section.
Any police officer may arrest without warrant any person offending in the officer's view against any provision of the Act — even where the maximum term is under 3 years. Bail is unaffected.
Every offence under the Act is arrestable and non-bailable.
Arrest without warrant only where reasonably suspected of s.16 or s.17 offences. Other offences follow CPC term defaults.
Specified offences (s.19 unlicensed moneylending, s.47 harassment) are expressly arrestable and non-bailable. Others follow CPC term defaults.
Police may arrest without warrant a person reasonably suspected of committing an offence under the Act.
Several sections carry their own arrest power; s.127 is a qualified power. Otherwise CPC term defaults apply.
Police may arrest without warrant a person offending in the officer's view against any provision of the Act.
CNB or police officers may arrest without warrant a person who has committed or is reasonably suspected of committing an offence under the Act — no in-view limit.
An officer may arrest without warrant a person they reasonably believe has committed an offence under the Act or regulations.
